title: Easy Thanksgiving Recipes That Take Up Absolutely No Oven Space
summary: Dishes for the stovetop, the slow-cooker, the air fryer, the Instant Pot and more.
body_markdown:
Advertisement


By Sharon Attia


Published Nov. 19, 2026


Updated Nov. 20, 2026


Oven space is famously precious on[Thanksgiving](https://cooking.nytimes.com/topics/thanksgiving) . Below are 17 recipes that skip the game of Tetris entirely. Some are cooked on the stovetop, others in a[slow-cooker](https://cooking.nytimes.com/article/easy-slow-cooker-recipes) , an[instant pot](https://cooking.nytimes.com/68861692-nyt-cooking/4441089-instant-pot-recipes) or an[air fryer](https://cooking.nytimes.com/68861692-nyt-cooking/42286557-air-fryer-recipes) . A few require no heat whatsoever.


## 1.[Potato Chip Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/794236702-potato-chip-mashed-potatoes?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Bryan Gardner for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Brett Regot.


Don’t let the casserole dish fool you — this recipe never touches the oven! Dan Pelosi likes to spread a thick layer of creamy, cheesy mashed potatoes into a 9-by-13 pan and top them with potato chips. But not just any potato chips; ones that have been sautéed in melted butter, toasted garlic and herbs.


Recipe: **[Potato Chip Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/794236702-potato-chip-mashed-potatoes?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 2.[Brussels Sprout Salad With Pomegranate and Pistachios](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026017-brussels-sprout-salad-with-pomegranate-and-pistachios?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Sheelah Prakash’s[tabbouleh](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1012585-tabbouleh?art=100000011272460) -inspired salad swaps the usual parsley and tomatoes for shaved brussels sprouts, scallions, mint, pomegranate seeds and roasted pistachios. Making the bulgur is the only cooking the recipe calls for. It’s perfect for potlucks or planners, as it can be assembled ahead of time and served at room temperature.


Recipe: **[Brussels Sprout Salad With Pomegranate and Pistachios](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026017-brussels-sprout-salad-with-pomegranate-and-pistachios?art=100000011272460)**


## 3.[Slow-Cooker Turkey Meatballs and Gravy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793138315-slow-cooker-turkey-meatballs-and-gravy?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


Sarah DiGregorio’s tender turkey meatballs and gravy are a great cost-saving alternative for anyone who doesn’t feel the need for a whole bird on Thanksgiving. The meatballs are seared in a skillet before moving to the slow cooker, where they hold on warm for several hours.


Recipe: **[Slow-Cooker Turkey Meatballs and Gravy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793138315-slow-cooker-turkey-meatballs-and-gravy?art=100000011272460)**


## 4.[Green Beans in Walnut Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/792082904-green-beans-in-walnut-vinaigrette?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


This is Kay Chun’s lighter, quicker alternative to the classic green bean casserole. Green beans are blanched and tossed in a vinaigrette made of white miso, lemon juice, minced shallot and finely chopped walnuts. Fresh dill is added before serving.


Recipe: **[Green Beans in Walnut Vinaigrette](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/792082904-green-beans-in-walnut-vinaigrette?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 5.[Coconut Creamed Corn](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762489782-coconut-creamed-corn?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Brett Regot.


Vegan? Lactose intolerant? Corn lover? This recipe from Hetty Lui McKinnon is for you. She uses coconut milk, instead of dairy, which brings out corn’s natural sweetness and cooks down beautifully with the grated kernels to create a creamy, porridge-like side dish.


Recipe: **[Coconut Creamed Corn](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762489782-coconut-creamed-corn?art=100000011272460)**


## 6.[No-Cook Cranberry Chutney](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015039-no-cook-cranberry-chutney?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


This no-cook cranberry sauce from Daniel Humm, the chef of Eleven Madison Park in New York, is bright, tart and oh-so-easy to make. Toss cranberries, sugar and orange zest into a stand mixer with a paddle attachment (a food processor won’t work), turn it on the lowest setting and come back in an hour to a glorious, ruby red, macerated chutney.


Recipe: **[No-Cook Cranberry Chutney](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015039-no-cook-cranberry-chutney?art=100000011272460)**


## 7.[Stovetop Mac and Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025254-stovetop-mac-and-cheese?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Genevieve Ko’s simple stovetop mac and cheese is creamy, silky and ready in 35 minutes. This recipe calls for a standard white sauce (butter, flour and milk) and grated, sharp yellow Cheddar — but it will work with any blend of cheeses. If you’ve got some random nubs in the fridge, grate ‘em up and chuck ‘em in!


Recipe: **[Stovetop Mac and Cheese](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1025254-stovetop-mac-and-cheese?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 8.[Ginger Scallion Broccoli Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/776098177-ginger-scallion-broccoli-salad?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Be like Kay Chun and blanch your broccoli. While it’s still warm, toss it with a vibrant dressing of scallions, oil, lemon juice, ginger and miso to help the vegetable soak up all of that flavor. One reader said the 20-minute recipe was “even better the next day.”


Recipe: **[Ginger Scallion Broccoli Salad](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/776098177-ginger-scallion-broccoli-salad?art=100000011272460)**


## 9.[No-Bake Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024588-no-bake-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Cyd Raftus McDowell.


Yossy Arefi’s pumpkin cheesecake looks down its nose at your oven. Her no-bake dessert is delightfully autumnal: It has a buttery Biscoff cookie crust, a fluffy and lightly spiced pumpkin filling and a cinnamon whipped cream topping. If you’ve got the fridge space, it can be made up to four days in advance.


Recipe: **[No-Bake Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024588-no-bake-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000011272460)**


## 10.[Crispy Ginger Sticky Rice](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024812-crispy-ginger-sticky-rice?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Samantha Seneviratne.


Inspired by a Cantonese dish that translates to “flavorful rice,” this dish from Genevieve Ko lives up to the name. In her recipe, chewy sticky rice (sometimes labeled sushi rice) is studded with bacon, mushrooms and crispy ginger. It’s a wonderful gluten-free and dairy-free alternative to buttery bread stuffing.


Recipe: **[Crispy Ginger Sticky Rice](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024812-crispy-ginger-sticky-rice?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 11.[Instant Pot Mashed Potatoes With Parmesan and Chives](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1018863-instant-pot-mashed-potatoes-with-sour-cream-and-chives?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times


Melissa Clark’s Instant Pot mash is ready in 20 minutes. Twenty minutes! Her recipe yields extra creamy potatoes (thanks to both butter and sour cream), which are then topped with a little Parmesan and fresh chives. (If you don’t have an Instant Pot, see Melissa’s[guide to making the best mashed potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/article/how-to-make-the-best-mashed-potatoes) .)


Recipe: **[Instant Pot Mashed Potatoes With Sour Cream and Chives](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1018863-instant-pot-mashed-potatoes-with-sour-cream-and-chives?art=100000011272460)**


## 12.[Spicy Peanut and Pumpkin Soup](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019759-spicy-peanut-and-pumpkin-soup?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Yewande Komolafe’s warming, 35-minute soup is an adaptation of a long-simmered stew common to much of West Africa. In her recipe, peanut butter, coconut milk and canned pumpkin temper the heat from the habanero or bird’s eye chile.


Recipe: **[Spicy Peanut and Pumpkin Soup](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019759-spicy-peanut-and-pumpkin-soup?art=100000011272460)**


## 13.[Air-Fryer Brussels Sprouts With Garlic, Balsamic and Soy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020126-air-fryer-brussels-sprouts-with-garlic-balsamic-and-soy?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


If there was ever a time to make the case for air-fryer supremacy, it may be on Thanksgiving with brussels sprouts. It achieves that ideal of a crunchy exterior and a tender interior. Melissa Clark throws in slivers of garlic, which crisp up, and then dresses the sprouts in a glossy mixture of lime juice, soy sauce and balsamic vinegar that’s been simmered until thickened.


Recipe: **[Air-Fryer Brussels Sprouts With Garlic, Balsamic and Soy](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020126-air-fryer-brussels-sprouts-with-garlic-balsamic-and-soy?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 14.[Cranberry Walnut Cheese Ball](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793137938-cranberry-walnut-cheese-ball?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Julia Gartland for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Yossy Arefi.


Yossy Arefi’s cheese ball is the ultimate make-ahead party trick: It’s easy to make, looks fun and will keep your hungry guests at bay as you finish up dinner. Her recipe features sharp Cheddar, dried cranberries, toasted walnuts or pecans, scallions, onion powder and Worcestershire sauce. Serve with crackers, chips or crudités (or all three!).


Recipe: **[Cranberry Walnut Cheese Ball](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793137938-cranberry-walnut-cheese-ball?art=100000011272460)**


## 15.[Slow-Cooker Cheddar Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/792690895-slow-cooker-cheddar-mashed-potatoes?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


Sarah DiGregorio’s recipe proves you don’t have to make your mashed potatoes immediately before serving. This Cheddar mash can be held on the warm setting for up to three hours before eating, saving you from the last-minute stress of getting the required side dish on the table in time.


Recipe: **[Slow-Cooker Cheddar Mashed Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/792690895-slow-cooker-cheddar-mashed-potatoes?art=100000011272460)**


## 16.[Glazed Parsley Carrots](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/4102-glazed-parsley-carrots?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Pierre Franey’s 15-minute recipe is a French classic. The dish is dead-simple: Cook carrots with some sugar, water, lemon juice and butter until they are tender and glazed with the melted sugar. C’est magnifique!


Recipe: **[Glazed Parsley Carrots](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/4102-glazed-parsley-carrots?art=100000011272460)**


Advertisement


## 17.[Simple Braised Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1014457-simple-braised-potatoes?art=100000011272460)


Credit...


Craig Lee for The New York Times


This potato recipe from Mark Bittman’s skips peeling, boiling and mashing and opts for braising potatoes in onions, garlic and a sprig of thyme or rosemary. As one reader commented: “Huge favorite! I’ve tried various potatoes. Yukon Gold are ideal for this, both in terms of flavor and structural integrity.”


Recipe: **[Simple Braised Potatoes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1014457-simple-braised-potatoes?art=100000011272460)**
